title: Capture
intro: When a chain's last liberty is filled, it comes off the board. That is a capture, and it is the only way a stone ever leaves.
A chain down to one liberty is said to be in atari. Say it out loud once and you will never forget it.

steps.instruction: The white stone has one liberty left. Take it.
steps.hint: Put your cursor on the white stone and look at where the ring is.
steps.explanation: Filling the last liberty lifts the stone off the board. It is now a prisoner, and at the end of the game it will be worth a point.

steps.instruction: Three white stones this time, and still one liberty between them. Take all three.
steps.hint: A chain shares its liberties. Find the single empty point they are all relying on.
steps.explanation: Chains are captured whole. It makes no difference whether it is one stone or twenty -- fill the last liberty and every stone in the chain comes off together. This is why a big chain with few liberties is far more dangerous to own than a small one with many.

steps.instruction: Two white stones, one liberty. Finish it.
steps.explanation: You have now captured a stone, a chain of three, and a chain of two. That is the whole of capturing. Everything harder in Go is this move, seen further ahead.

outro: Good. You know how to take stones off the board.
The fastest way to get comfortable with it is a game where capturing is the only thing that matters -- Capture Go. Pip plays it in the park, endlessly, and loses cheerfully. Go and find him.
